name: Keycloak
description: Self-hosted identity provider (OIDC, OAuth2, SAML). Run one login for your other apps: create a realm, register a client, and point any OIDC-capable app at it. Production mode with a Postgres store, so realms, clients and user accounts survive a restart. Sign in at /admin/ with the generated admin password, and read the guidance on that field before you deploy: it carries the post-install hardening steps and a warning you cannot undo. Keycloak keeps SMTP per realm in its own database rather than in environment variables, so this greffon cannot inherit the platform SMTP integration, and password reset stays off until you set mail per realm. First boot runs a Quarkus build step and then a schema migration before serving, roughly 30 to 40 seconds on an unloaded machine and minutes on a busy one.

value.title: Admin username
value.description: Master-realm administrator, created on first boot only. Do not leave this blank: Keycloak then invents an account called temp-admin instead, and there is no second chance because the bootstrap only runs when no admin exists.

value.title: Admin password
value.description: Password for the admin console, minted by the platform. Reveal it with the eye icon and save it somewhere before you deploy. Do NOT regenerate this field after the instance exists: Keycloak sets the admin password on first boot only, so regenerating replaces the stored copy of the real password without changing the one Keycloak accepts, and you lose console access for good. Right after your first login, harden the master realm, because Keycloak's defaults are permissive and none of them can be set from this form: turn on Brute force detection under Realm settings, Security defenses (without it the token endpoint accepts unlimited password guesses), turn on user event and admin event storage under Realm settings, Events (bearing in mind that the client IP recorded against a login is taken from a proxy header a client can set, so treat it as a hint rather than evidence), then create a permanent admin account and delete the temporary one Keycloak bootstraps. This account owns every realm on this instance.

value.title: Database password
value.description: Generated by the platform at instance creation. Internal to this instance: Keycloak and Postgres share it, nothing else reads it. Do NOT regenerate it after the instance has been created. Postgres only reads POSTGRES_PASSWORD when it initialises an empty data directory, so the stored role keeps the old password while Keycloak starts with the new one and cannot connect. Changing it needs an ALTER ROLE inside the database, which the platform does not do for you.
